setup: Lie on your back on a mat, knees bent
Feet flat, about hip width apart
execution: Breathe out and curl your shoulder up
Bring one shoulder toward the opposite knee
Lower back stays on the mat
Lower slowly; do all reps, then switch
faults: Don't pull on your head or neck
Don't just swing the elbow across

notes: Keep the hands light behind the head; the trunk does the lifting, not the arms.
A short range is fine: the shoulder blade only needs to lift off the mat.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Dead bug
regressions.reason: Trunk control on the back without any curling; easier on the neck.

regressions.name: Crunch
regressions.reason: Straight curl-up with no twist; learn the short range first.

progressions.name: Bicycle crunch
progressions.reason: Alternating sides with the legs moving; more demanding.

progressions.name: Cable woodchop
progressions.reason: Loaded rotation on a stack, so it progresses in small steps.

substitutions.name: Cable woodchop
substitutions.reason: Standing, loaded rotation for the obliques.

substitutions.name: Side plank
substitutions.reason: Obliques held still instead of curled; no spinal flexion.

substitutions.name: Pallof press
substitutions.reason: Obliques resist twisting; no flexion or rotation.

substitutions.name: Cable side bend
substitutions.reason: Loaded side-bending for the obliques on a stack.

guideBrief.cameraNote: View from just beyond the feet, camera raised about 30° above the floor so the diagonal path of the shoulder toward the opposite knee is clear. Mat along the floor.

keyPositions.label: Start
keyPositions.describe: Lying on the back, knees bent about 90°, feet flat. Fingertips lightly by the ears, elbows wide. Head and shoulders resting on the mat.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Upper back curled up and turned so the right shoulder moves toward the left knee. Right shoulder blade off the mat, lower back still down. Chin a fist's width from the chest; elbows still wide.

ikHints: Feet and pelvis stay fixed on the mat
Hands stay by the ears; they don't pull the head
emphasise: The shoulder travels diagonally, not just the elbow
Lower back stays on the mat
